notes.title: Developer’s Log: Q1 2025
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Welcome to our first update of 2025! This time around we'll cover the latest progress update, my thoughts on release date, and some tubular tunes from the main composers. Let's jump right in!

[hr][/hr] 
Progress Report
Fortunately the personal issues that were plaguing me the last few months are all but over. I've been able to focus more on development and have even completed the semi-optional areas I mentioned before. Now there's only the last section of the game to do -- think the Return to Midgar and Northern Cave in FF7. To be conservative I'll still say the main story is at 90% completion, but I'm more optimistic about completing the game this year. 

In terms of the launch date, I'll decide by next update in Q2 if a release this year is best. As mentioned last time, there needs to be some consideration for post-production like polishing, QA, marketing, etc. This being my first major game release, I'd rather err on the side of caution to ensure a quality game is out on Day 1... not a buggy mess that needs several patches.

[hr][/hr] 
Original Soundtrack
I'm glad to say this is progressing smoothly as well and believe the full OST of 40+ songs should be ready by the time the main story is finished. That's quite a feat for our composers considering they only started on it 6 months ago!

Here's are a few samples of the soundtrack by our two main composers. The first is the Main City theme (Torlukos City) and the other the Boss Battle 1 theme. Enjoy!

[previewyoutube=UB2q7YTt_ko;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]











For the next update I'll be sharing the Main Theme of One Fenix Down, with vocals by the one and only Emi Evans! Kickstarter backers will have an exclusive preview of it on the KS page -- check it out!

[hr][/hr] 
Asset Development
Lastly I want to highlight some other characters and battlers in development! From a humble blacksmith to an unknown ninja to some barbaric-looking characters:

notes.title: Developer’s Log: Q4 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Happy holidays and a happy 2025! It's been an eventful 2024 for One Fenix Down, from launching our Steam page and demo to funding a successful Kickstarter! As always I wanted to share the latest developments with our game along with the assets in development. So without further ado... 

[hr][/hr] 
Progress Report
As any aspiring game developer would admit, the hardest part about making a game is arguably the discipline of sitting down and doing the work day after day after day. Especially when life throws you some serious curveballs. Such is the case with me which has unfortunately slowed down production these past few months. However, I have been able to finish many semi-optional areas leading up to the final dungeon despite the setbacks.

Overall I'd estimate the main story to be at 90% completion. This isn't a huge step-up from the 85% estimate I had during the Kickstarter, but rest assured progress is being made. As such I still believe a Q4 2025 launch date is doable. The main variable will be the time needed to polish and quality check the final game -- I'd rather push back the launch than release something rushed out the door.

[hr][/hr] 
Asset Development
Last time we highlighted the original soundtrack from achieving our Kickstarter goal. This time I want to share some of the characters and battlers in development -- from dastardly bosses to important side characters!

notes.title: Developer’s Log: Q3 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

I'm excited to share some updates over the past few months! From our Kickstarter being funded in only 3 days, to samples and guest appearances of our OST, to the latest snippets from the game, I've got some neat things to share for this devlog update! 

[hr][/hr] 
Kickstarter 230% Funded!
Wow, what a journey that was. I still am blown away at the results. 230% funded overall and hitting our funding goal in 3 days?! Outstanding. And as a bonus, we hit our stretch goal to bring Emi Evans onboard to write and perform the main theme of our game!

I'll leave Late Pledges available for another month in case anyone wants to grab One Fenix Down now on discount and with the digital strategy guide included!

Link to the Kickstarter: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/rcdunn/one-fenix-down-a-retro-inspired-turn-based-rpg

[hr][/hr] 
Original Soundtrack Sample
Thanks to achieving our Kickstarter goal, we've already begun production of the original soundtrack for One Fenix Down! We even added a third composer to help with a few additional tracks to ensure they're all completed on time. In total I expect the collection to be approximately 50 original songs!

Eventually I will share the songs over YouTube and will likely offer an option to purchase the HQ OST via Steam. For now, here is a sample of the OST with an amazing track by Thomas J Peters that plays during a few pivotal moments in the game:

notes.title: Special Update: Demo and Kickstarter Launch
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

I'm happy to announce that we'll be releasing our game demo and launching our Kickstarter over the next week!


Steam Demo/Prologue - July 25
Beginning Thursday you'll be able to play our demo on Steam! This demo is actually a hybrid game demo and preview of the main story. Half will be devoted to content not in the actual game while the other half introduces the prologue and first ~15 mins. of the actual game. 

The reason for this split is that the two pair rather well. The demo features a vertical slice of gameplay elements you'll discover throughout the game including party swapping, equipment upgrades, on-map encounters, and event-based instant victory. Since the story in the demo is canon, it felt natural to extend it into the prologue (the beginning of the full game) so that players can see the conclusion of the events.


Kickstarter - August 1
The following Thursday, on August 1st, the Kickstarter will finally be launched!

Our focus with the campaign will be to finance two talented composers, bringing them on to the team to create the official One Fenix Down OST. We even have a special guest who will be collaborating on the main theme provided that we can hit our first stretch goal.

We're excited to show off our campaign soon and the various rewards people can earn by donating towards our KS goal. Here's the link to our page in case you haven't already followed it:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/rcdunn/one-fenix-down-a-retro-inspired-turn-based-rpg

(As I type this we have exactly 111 KS followers... a little on the nose with our game nameːsteamhappyː)

Demo/Prologue Preview
Play as the mysterious Chichioku and the steadfast Iron Guard as they witness the invasion of the Kingdom of Torloria. Utilize mid- to late-game skills and mechanics as you control the party of veterans. Try to unravel the identity and purpose of these invaders -- why pillage this peaceful kingdom? Why now?

Here are a few samples from the demo:

notes.title: Developer’s Log: May - June 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Hope you all are enjoying the summer (or winter for those of you down under). I have some mixed news to share for this devlog update. And to keep with the habit, I'll include some of the latest snippets of work I've done over the last month.


Kickstarter/Demo Delayed ːsteamfacepalmː
I was a little overly optimistic about the timeline launch for both of these. I'm now aiming for next month, but it's unfortunately out of my hands to an extent. You see, one of our artist has some personal issues that's preventing a certain piece from being completed. Otherwise the demo and Kickstarter page are ready to go, but without that last piece I'd be launching something that's 99% ready which doesn't sit right with me. Frankly I don't know how AAA titles do it (shots fired).

So until that last piece is finished, we'll just need to sit tight. I would, however, appreciate any additional Kickstarter pre-launch follows!

Link to the Kickstarter: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/rcdunn/one-fenix-down-a-retro-inspired-turn-based-rpg


A Wild [Composer] Has Appeared!
As a solo developer you're regularly approached by individuals interested in collaboration. I've had a few composers contact me over the years, and have really wanted to start work on an OST with them, but knew that I had to cover the artwork first.

Now that the Kickstarter is a real thing, I've been narrowing it down to two composers I'd really like to work with, and have been in contact with both of them.

The first is YouFulca, an exceptional composer who has been creating professional JRPG music for over a decade. We hope to add him to the team, provided that the Kickstarter funding goal is met! He will be focusing on battle and boss soundtracks for the OST.

The second is Thomas J. Peters who has composed some wonderful soundtracks for other indie games such as the JRPG Numina. Like YouFulca, we hope to add him to the team! He will be focusing on town, field, and event soundtracks for the OST.

Provided that we don't reach our Kickstarter goal, I will try to scrounge up a little to afford at least 1 or 2 songs from these talented composers.


Main Story and Gameplay Snippets
Fortunately I have been making progress with the main story and would estimate that it is about ~90% complete at this point. On a personal note, I took a step down from some of my job responsibilities to invest more time and focus on game development. As a result, I'm tearing through a lot of the content (some optional) leading up to the final dungeon.

notes.title: Developer’s Log: March - April 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Thanks for checking out the latest ONE FENIX DOWN bi-monthly dev log. I'm a little early for this one as I wanted to share some exciting news -- we're launching a Kickstarter campaign later this year! And as part of that, we'll release our (likely) final demo of ONE FENIX DOWN on Steam! You can read more about these down below. I've also included some gameplay snippets of work I've done over the last month.


Kickstarter!
As mentioned in the last update, I've decided to go ahead and create a Kickstarter page. My intention is to launch this late spring/early summer provided that the final demo will be available. Although it's still a few months away, I would greatly appreciate any pre-launch follows on the page below.

Link to the Kickstarter: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/rcdunn/one-fenix-down-a-retro-inspired-turn-based-rpg

Also previously mentioned, ONE FENIX DOWN is pretty far into development and has been a self-sufficient project/hobby thus far. So why turn to Kickstarter now? Well, there were a few elements that I would have loved to enhance but were outside of my budget, such as having an original soundtrack and gorgeous pixel art backdrops for certain scenes. For this reason the team has decided to try a small Kickstarter campaign so we can aim for a more polished release. 


Upcoming Demo
Those who've been following ONE FENIX DOWN on Twitter and itch.io may already know that we had an earlier demo release just last year. It was a ~30 minute slice of gameplay elements, as well as showcasing the canon story with a prologue that won't be in the main game.

The Steam demo will be much like this one, but with some enhancements including final artwork (16-bit sprites), a new UI, and some rework to combat. For the majority of you who haven't played it, I think you'll be in for a treat! Most people seem to really enjoy it even as a standalone story.

I'll share an update next time on a hopefully more concrete date for the demo's release.

notes.title: Developer’s Log: January - February 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Firstly, I want to say a big thank you to all those who have wishlisted and followed ONE FENIX DOWN. The Steam page was launched just two weeks ago, and I’m overwhelmed by the interest and support you’ve all shown. 

I figured the least I could do for the hundreds of you wanting to try the game is create transparency with this developer’s log, sharing my thoughts and progress every 1-2 months. Without further ado…


State of the Game
Overall the main story of ONE FENIX DOWN is approximately 85% complete. Although it sounds nearly complete, I’d estimate the average player will take 35-40 hours to finish it. Therefore that last 15% is still a sizeable chunk outstanding.

Artwork is also making progress, although I’d estimate that being closer to 60% complete. Our pixel artists are hard at work with the next batch of battlers, and here’s a taste:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/2852e6c41a5c01ae735e8b63dd2b2e9893e4f7b7.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/af2fc345327e8067bf46913c643534b6ff21abfc.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/d2d9eac5487044110b7c759ece61e0da180bb9ad.png

We’re also constantly getting new portraits from our artist for the 100+ characters in the game, and here’s a sample of those as well:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/ecdf5efd02cb7706e1a4bc633ddcd0e88a0452f2.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/0029a4922f37a80aff8dab8666b230172ca515e3.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44872014/72d8e06f584d106d257877b77510c2cee1367bf7.jpg


Q&A from Social Media
I created a few reddit and X/Twitter posts to share the news of the Steam page. There were a few questions that popped up more than once, or garnered a bit of attention, so I wanted to share those here.


Q: When will the game be released? 
A: TBD, however the ambition is to aim for a 2nd half of 2025 release. 

Q: Is there a demo available? 
A: We had an old demo with placeholder art, but that is no longer being circulated. Current plans are to release a final demo for a future Steam Next Fest, likely during the October one later this year. 

Q: Why has development taken nearly a decade? Is anyone else working on the game?
A: It's a fair question as someone probably could have done it in half the time. Honestly it mainly started out as a fun side project, and since I had a full time job I'd only work on it here and there. It wasn't until after I had 30+ hours of playtime and a lot of great feedback from testers when I decided to polish it up and get it to Steam. 
Although I’m a solo dev, I can’t take credit for the artwork from the talented artists I've commissioned! The main contributor for the pixel art is a Japanese artist named vibrato, and for the portraits it's a comic artist who goes by BeanyCoffee. Shout out to Vit-Tunissy who has been making some great enemies to complement vibrato’s style.

Q: How do characters progress? Is it standard leveling and gearing up?
A: Leveling will be like standard old-school JRPGs where enemies give EXP, and new skills are tied to levels. There will also be optional skills, such as weapon proficiencies, that can be purchased using class points. Gear can be purchased in towns, but the most powerful items will need to be won via boss fights or found by exploring dungeons.

Q: Party members come and go, and don’t stay in the main party? (In response to my post)
A: Yes, party members come and go mainly due to story reasons -- they have their own objectives and it doesn't make sense for them to follow Fenix initially. Most party members end up in the final party though; there will be late-game mechanics like how the Phoenix Cave was done in FFVI where you'll need to split into multiple parties.

Q: Will this be available for Steam Deck and Switch? 
A: Steam Deck will be tested prior to release. Switch will likely not be available at release, but it is an ambition to eventually release on the console.

Q: What languages will be available? 
A: Besides English I can’t make any promises. There is a desire to translate into several languages such as Japanese, Spanish, and Portuguese just to name a few. However, I’m already over budget to see the game to completion, speaking of which…


Considering a Small Kickstarter
Although I started this game way back in 2016 as a passion project/side hobby, it's amazing to see it drastically evolve into the full-fledged RPG that it is today. A few years back I made a budget for replacing the placeholder assets with some top-notch artwork. Well, I’ve long since burned through that budget, but am happy to have saved up and self-funded the essentials up until now. Honestly, RPGs can be quite expensive with all the characters, enemies, animations, map tiles, and so on. Looking at the results though, it was worth every penny.

That being said, there were a few elements that I would have loved to enhance, such as an own original soundtrack and gorgeous pixel art backdrops for certain scenes. For this reason I’m mulling over trying a small crowdsource campaign on Kickstarter in the next few months so we can still aim for a 2025 release. With some stretch goals in place, this may also be a great way to release the game with multiple language support and/or a Switch version near release as some folks have inquired about.



That’s all for now. Thanks again for the support!

-RC
